source_text: Errat etiam honestorum cautio, quae naturalibus rebus verecundiae praetendit umbracula. Tu ergo ipse reliquias ciborum, quas certe confiteris non pertinere ad libidinem, sub oculis depelle populorum; immo ut dogmati tuo auctoritatem concilies exemplo, in Ecclesia facito omnia, quae ad nutum dicis fieri voluntatis, contentusque operam solius commixtionis occulere, a qua, et olim proposito, forsitan, et nunc senio destitisti, dicito ad grande sacrilegium pertinere, si res quae Deum conditorem habet, publicum vitet aspectum. Comede igitur in foro, aut in synagogis, in quibus disputationes tuae personant; et cum vestimenta sub sole torrido fuerint, oneri, tegens illam tantummodo corporis tui partem quam diabolus movit, reliqua nudus incedito; quia pronuntias ingratum esse et profanum, si quid tegatur quod Dei operibus adscribitur. Quod cum horum nihil facis (si tamen non proficiendo feceris), ipsis operibus confirmas alterum de duobus, aut omnia ista ad diabolum pertinere, quae non exsequeris sub conspectu publico; aut dogma vestrum, si non corde, vel ventre tuo teste cecidisse.
pass_a_gloss: The caution of honorable people also errs, which holds out shades of reverence before natural things. You yourself therefore drive away under the eyes of the peoples the remnants of foods, which you certainly confess do not belong to lust; nay, that you may win authority for your dogma by example, do in the Church all things which you say are done at the nod of the will, and, content to hide the work of mingling alone, from which you have perhaps desisted both by an old resolve and now by old age, say that it belongs to a great sacrilege if a thing which has God as founder avoids public sight. Eat therefore in the forum, or in the synagogues in which your disputations resound; and when garments have been under a torrid sun, as a burden, covering only that part of your body which the devil moved, walk naked for the rest; because you pronounce it ungrateful and profane if anything is covered which is ascribed to God's works. Which, since you do none of these things (if nevertheless you have not done them by making progress), you confirm by the works themselves one of two things: either that all those things belong to the devil which you do not carry out under public sight; or that your dogma has fallen, if not with the heart, at least with your belly as witness.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: Then respectable people are also wrong to take care to screen natural functions with modesty. So you yourself should evacuate the remains of your food—which you certainly admit do not belong to lust—under the people’s eyes. Indeed, to lend your doctrine authority by your example, perform in church everything you say happens at the will’s command. Be content to hide only the act of sexual union, from which you long ago abstained by resolution and perhaps now also through old age. Say that it is a great sacrilege for anything whose creator is God to avoid public view. Eat, then, in the marketplace or in the meeting places where your arguments resound. And when clothes become a burden under a scorching sun, cover only that part of your body that the devil has moved, and walk about otherwise naked. For you pronounce it ungrateful and profane to cover anything assigned to God’s works. Since you do none of these things—unless further progress has already brought you to do them—your very conduct confirms one of two conclusions: either everything you do not perform in public view belongs to the devil, or your doctrine has fallen, on the testimony, if not of your heart, at least of your belly.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
